notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Thursday 26 November; the EGX is shut on Friday and Saturday. Brent and Asian stocks are Friday-morning prices; US markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen for a shortened session on Friday. The CBE's dollar rate is EnterpriseAM's 26 November market table. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Thursday prices, the latest on its page. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Thursday's index levels for the EGX30, EGX70, EGX100, EGX33 and EGX35-LV, which no source we opened had published (Amwal Al Ghad's 26 November report is not online; Arab Finance's pages show only headlines), so the index cards show Wednesday's closes and the EGX30 tile uses EnterpriseAM's rounded 0.5% fall; Thursday's flows in EGP; the odds of a December Fed hike (96.2% and 99% in two Investing.com articles); US tariff rates on China (20% per Al Jazeera on 25 November, up to 40% per EnterpriseAM on 26 November); Brent's weekly gain (4.5% or 4.6%) and November fall (nearly 18% or nearly 20%); Friday's Nikkei move.
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Friday and show Thursday 26 November as the latest session.

items: Suez Canal revenue doubles to $593 mn so far in November, from $295 mn a year earlier, as major shipping lines return → more dollar income eases pressure on the pound and the current account.
Orascom Construction closes its OCI deal, issuing 97.2 mn new shares, but misses its 24 November listing date → the enlarged company's new shares still await admission to the EGX and ADX.
US core PCE inflation rises to 3.3%, the highest since November 2023, and markets price a December Fed hike at 98% → higher US rates keep pressure on emerging-market flows and the pound.
The EGX30 falls 0.68% to 50,538.66 as local investors sell; the pound weakens to 54.76 per dollar at the CBE → turnover stays thin at EGP 6.2 bn, 43.3% below the 90-day average.

The Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Hodeidah port, and the Houthis threaten all Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah → a wider Red Sea war raises the risk to Suez Canal traffic and Egypt's shipping costs.
The AI sell-off returns: Seoul's Kospi falls 6.16% and Taiwan 4.94% on Wednesday after the Nasdaq drops 1.5% → doubts over AI returns and new US tariff threats weigh on global risk appetite.
The EGX30 edges up 0.34% to 50,885.33 as Sidpec jumps 5.4% → the index is still 10.2% below its 6 September peak.
Retail investors cover only 0.19x of Misr Life's public tranche on day one → the soft start tests demand for the state's biggest listing of the year.
The EGX30 rebounds 1.44% to 50,711.96 on Monday and small caps jump 3.41%, recovering part of Sunday's sell-off → every stock in the 21-stock table except Emaar Misr rises as global markets steady.

Misr Life Insurance opens its IPO book at EGP 12.00 to 13.60 a share, valuing it at EGP 60 to 68 bn → the whole range sits below the EGP 13.82 fair value set by its adviser; trading is due around 3 December.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang and the Nasdaq jumps 6.5%, its best day since April 2025; Taiwan rises about 9% on Tuesday → the AI trade revives after last week's rout, lifting risk appetite worldwide.
Brent falls 3.46% to $89.37, its lowest close since 31 August, as Libya restarts the Sharara pipeline → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill.

The EGX30 drops 2.85% to 49,989.79 on Sunday and small caps fall 5.55%, as local investors sell after Wall Street's correction → foreigners are the only net buyers; turnover stays 40.4% below its 90-day average.
Three LNG cargoes bound for Egypt divert to Europe, and fertiliser makers pay 50% more for gas at $12.75/mmBtu → Europe outbids Cairo for scarce cargoes, raising costs for energy-hungry industry.
US stock futures jump 2.2% on Monday after the S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday into a correction → a rebound abroad could steady the EGX after Sunday's sell-off.
Tankers are set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi refinery → Gulf attacks keep oil's risk premium alive; Brent holds near $92.7.
Iran strikes US air-defence sites in Bahrain and tankers are hit near Hormuz on Saturday → the Gulf war widens, keeping oil, shipping and insurance risk high for Egypt.
Goldman Sachs sees the CBE holding at 20% until late Q1 2027, then cutting 700 bp by 2028 → it calls the pound more than 30% undervalued and sees no external financing gap through FY2029/30.
Misr Life Insurance, which earned EGP 5.8 bn in 2025, targets a 70% payout ahead of its EGX debut in early December → a large, high-dividend state listing deepens the market.
Orascom Construction breaks ground on Jordan's $6.7 bn Aqaba-Amman water project → the project adds to its backlog before its merger shares list on 24 November.

stories.h: Attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery kills a worker as oil climbs
stories.what: An aerial projectile hits Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on the Red Sea, which can process up to 400,000 barrels a day, killing one worker and halting some operations. The Saudi-led coalition blames the Houthis, who a day earlier claimed attacks on Ras Tanura and the ports of Jeddah and Jazan. In Kuwait, two Italians die from debris as Iranian drones are intercepted. Brent rises to $96.61 on Friday morning after its highest close since 6 November.
stories.why: The Houthis widen attacks on Saudi energy sites during the war on Iran.
stories.aff: Oil supply, Red Sea ports and shipping.
stories.eg: Higher oil prices lift Egypt's fuel import bill, and Red Sea risk weighs on shipping.

key.l: period OPEC+ is likely to keep targets unchanged

stories.h: OPEC+ set to hold output targets on Sunday as oil heads for a weekly gain
stories.what: OPEC+ is likely to keep its output targets for at least the first quarter of 2027 at its meeting on Sunday, two sources tell Reuters. WTI rises 2.5% to $85.78 on Friday from Wednesday's close. Oil is on track to end a three-week losing streak, though Hormuz tanker traffic is recovering and the IEA expects a fourth-quarter surplus.
stories.why: Gulf attacks outweigh signs of ample supply.
stories.aff: Oil prices and Egypt's fuel subsidy bill.
stories.eg: Firm oil prices keep pressure on the budget.

stories.h: Chinese stocks surge on Beijing's support pledges; US futures rise
stories.what: China's CSI 300 jumps 3.5% to 4,036.09 and the Shanghai Composite 3.2% after Beijing pledges more support and cuts margin requirements from 30 November; Seoul's Kospi gains 4.1%. US stock futures rise ahead of a shortened Friday session. President Trump calls the upward revision of US third-quarter growth to 4.3% fake and demands an investigation. Proposed US tariffs on 14 trading partners could take effect as early as January.
stories.why: Beijing acts to steady its markets after the AI sell-off.
stories.aff: Global risk appetite and emerging-market flows.
stories.eg: Calmer markets support flows into Egyptian assets.

stories.h: EGX30 slips 0.5% as Telecom Egypt falls and Orascom rebounds
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.5% on Thursday on turnover of EGP 6.4 bn, 40.9% below the 90-day average, leaving it up 20.3% this year. International investors are the only net buyers. Raya Holding (+5.2%), Orascom Construction (+3.5%) and Edita (+2.9%) lead the gainers; Telecom Egypt (-2.4%), Qalaa (-1.8%) and e-finance (-1.6%) lead the losers. The CBE quotes the dollar at 54.76.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause.
stories.eg: The market drifts lower in thin trade before the Misr Life listing.
stories.names: Orascom Construction, Edita (up); Telecom Egypt, Qalaa (down).

key.l: Misr Life retail cover on day one

stories.h: Misr Life's institutional book closes today; the final price is due Saturday
stories.what: Institutional subscriptions for Misr Life Insurance close on Friday and retail subscriptions on Monday, with the final price due on Saturday and trading on or around Thursday 3 December. Retail investors covered the public tranche 0.19x on day one, ordering about 7.09 mn of 37.5 mn shares. Separately, Egypt detains the driver in Wednesday's Ring Road fuel tanker fire, which killed 31; the CBE directs banks to give EGP 60 mn to victims' families.
stories.why: The state sells part of a large insurer.
stories.aff: IPO demand and the state's divestment plan.
stories.eg: The institutional book will decide the pricing.
stories.egx: Neutral until the price is set.

key.l: Xin Feng Ming polyester complex in Sokhna

stories.h: Xin Feng Ming breaks ground on an $800 mn polyester complex; Sisi meets Qatar's emir
stories.what: China's Xin Feng Ming starts work on the $280 mn first phase of an $800 mn polyester complex in Sokhna, with capacity of 360,000 tons a year rising to 1 mn tons. President Sisi meets Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim in Cairo to discuss trade, investment, energy and the Gaza ceasefire.
stories.why: Egypt courts Chinese and Gulf investment for industry.
stories.eg: More export-oriented manufacturing in the SCZone.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for textile and petrochemical names.

stories.h: Gold rebounds 1.8% from a 15-month low; 21K in Egypt rises 1.9%
stories.what: Spot gold rises 1.8% to $3,629.87 late on Thursday after falling more than 3% on Wednesday to its lowest close since September 2025. It is still on course for a third monthly decline of more than 6%. In Egypt, Banky's 21K price rises EGP 105, or 1.90%, to EGP 5,645 a gram.
stories.why: Bargain hunters return after the sharp drop, while Fed hike bets cap gains.
stories.eg: Local prices recover part of this week's losses.
